---
title: "S-parameters with Palace"
description: "Compute the S-parameters of two launchers joined by a coplanar waveguide with Palace's Driven solver, read them back and write a Touchstone file."
scgsim-kind: "course"
scgsim-status: "CONVERGING"
scgsim-id: "docs/course/palace-driven"
---

Palace's Driven solver drives each port of a layout in turn, frequency by
frequency, and returns the S-parameters: how much of the wave sent into one
port comes back from it and how much comes out of each other port. On this
page the layout is a through line: two launchers of the OrcaPen SC PDK,
each a 150 µm pad that tapers into a coplanar waveguide (CPW), joined by
900 µm of that CPW. Each launcher is a 50 Ω port, and the sweep runs from 2
to 10 GHz. The script prints:

```text
P1 chip/o_lumped_left: LumpedPort, R 50.0 ohm, excitation 1: port 1 of the S-matrix, driven from chip/SIGNAL to chip/GROUND
P2 chip/o_lumped_right: LumpedPort, R 50.0 ohm, excitation 2: port 2 of the S-matrix, driven from chip/SIGNAL to chip/GROUND
Status: completed
Port 1 driven: 4 frequencies solved, error 1.2e-06
Port 2 driven: 4 frequencies solved, error 4.6e-06
 2.0 GHz  |S11| = -41.08 dB  |S21| = -0.0004 dB  arg S21 =  -11.118 deg
 4.0 GHz  |S11| = -35.38 dB  |S21| = -0.0015 dB  arg S21 =  -22.235 deg
 6.0 GHz  |S11| = -32.39 dB  |S21| = -0.0030 dB  arg S21 =  -33.352 deg
 8.0 GHz  |S11| = -30.67 dB  |S21| = -0.0045 dB  arg S21 =  -44.469 deg
10.0 GHz  |S11| = -29.81 dB  |S21| = -0.0058 dB  arg S21 =  -55.589 deg
```

Almost all the power goes through: |S21| stays within 0.006 dB of 0 dB, and
at most 0.1 % of the power comes back (|S11| at most −29.8 dB). The phase
of S21 falls in proportion to the frequency, as a line's delay makes it.
[Read the result](#read-the-result) takes the numbers apart. The script also
writes all 81 frequencies to the Touchstone file `launchers.s2p`, which
circuit simulators read.

You need the installation of First simulation: SCGSim with its `palace`
extra, the OrcaPen SC PDK, Palace 0.18.1, and `SCGSIM_PALACE_EXECUTABLE` set
to the `palace` command ([First simulation](../start/first-simulation.qmd#palace-executable)).

## The layout {#the-layout}

A port sits on a port sheet: a rectangle on a port layer that joins the
port's signal metal to its reference metal, here a pad to the ground across
the 85 µm gap behind it. The sheet must reach a little way into both metals,
so that SCGSim can find the two conductors it joins. The PDK's `launcher`
draws a sheet that only touches its pad and the ground edge to edge, so this
layout draws its own two sheets, each reaching 10 nm into the pad and into
the ground. Save this as `launchers.py` in your study project:

```python
import gdsfactory as gf
from orcapen_sc_pdk.ports import add_driven_lumped_port
from orcapen_sc_pdk.tech import LAYER

LINE_UM = 900.0  # the CPW between the two launchers
PAD_UM = 150.0  # the launcher's square pad
TAPER_UM = 150.0  # its taper from the pad to the CPW
BACK_GAP_UM = 85.0  # the gap behind the pad, which the port sheet spans
LANDING_UM = 0.01  # how far each sheet reaches into the pad and into the ground


def launcher_to_launcher() -> gf.Component:
    """Two PDK launchers joined by a 900 µm CPW on a 1870 × 900 µm die, a port sheet behind each pad."""
    chip = gf.Component()
    # The launcher's own sheet only touches its pad and the ground, so it goes to a layer nothing reads.
    launcher = gf.get_component(
        "launcher",
        cpw_xs="cpw_6_7_6",
        sim_boundary_layer=(250, 0),
        curve_sampling="simulation",
    )
    left = chip << launcher
    left.move(origin=left.ports["o_neck"].center, destination=(-LINE_UM / 2, 0.0))
    right = chip << launcher
    right.rotate(180)
    right.move(origin=right.ports["o_neck"].center, destination=(LINE_UM / 2, 0.0))
    line = chip << gf.components.straight(
        length=LINE_UM, cross_section=gf.get_cross_section("cpw_6_7_6")
    )
    line.move(origin=line.ports["o1"].center, destination=left.ports["o_neck"].center)
    chip << gf.components.rectangle(
        size=(1870.0, 900.0), centered=True, layer=LAYER.D0_SUBSTRATE_AREA
    )

    # A port sheet across the gap behind each pad, from the ground to the pad.
    pad_back = LINE_UM / 2 + TAPER_UM + PAD_UM
    for name, side in (("o_lumped_left", -1.0), ("o_lumped_right", 1.0)):
        x0, x1 = sorted(
            (side * (pad_back - LANDING_UM), side * (pad_back + BACK_GAP_UM + LANDING_UM))
        )
        y = PAD_UM / 2
        chip.add_polygon(
            [(x0, -y), (x1, -y), (x1, y), (x0, y)], layer=LAYER.D0_TOP_SIM_BOUNDARY
        )
        add_driven_lumped_port(
            chip,
            name=name,
            center=(side * (pad_back + BACK_GAP_UM / 2), 0.0),
            orientation=0.0 if side < 0 else 180.0,
            layer=LAYER.D0_TOP_SIM_BOUNDARY,
        )

    # What the plan reads: the signal metal, the ground metal and the two sheets.
    chip.info["component_semantics"] = {
        "schema_version": 2,
        "conductor_regions": [
            {
                "semantic_id": "SIGNAL",
                "level": "D0_TOP_M1",
                "gds_layer": tuple(LAYER.D0_TOP_M1_DRAW),
                "geometry": {
                    "geometry_source": "gds_polygon",
                    "selector_point_um": (0.0, 0.0),
                },
            },
            {
                "semantic_id": "GROUND",
                "level": "D0_TOP_M1",
                "gds_layer": tuple(LAYER.D0_TOP_GROUND_MASK),
            },
        ],
        "ports": [
            {
                "name": name,
                "layer": tuple(LAYER.D0_TOP_SIM_BOUNDARY),
                "target_layer": "D0_TOP_M1",
            }
            for name in ("o_lumped_left", "o_lumped_right")
        ],
    }
    return chip
```

The CPW is the PDK's `cpw_6_7_6`: a 7 µm signal line in 6 µm gaps. The
launchers and the line form one piece of signal metal, `SIGNAL`; the rest of
the chip's top face is the ground, `GROUND`. The chip is 1870 × 900 µm of
silicon, 500 µm thick, with 0.1 µm of aluminium, from the PDK's single-die
layer stack.

## The script {#the-script}

Save this as `launcher_s_parameters.py` next to `launchers.py`:

```python
import cmath
import math
import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4

import orcapen_sc_pdk
from orcapen_sc_pdk import get_material_records, validate_interface_preset_records
from orcapen_sc_pdk.tech import get_single_die_layer_stack
from scgsim.geometry import GeometryPlan, LumpedPort
from scgsim.palace import DrivenSim, Linear, resolve_palace_result

from launchers import launcher_to_launcher

# 1. The layout and its plan: the signal and ground Nets, the vacuum, and thin lossy films (PDK presets).
orcapen_sc_pdk.activate()
plan = GeometryPlan(
    component=launcher_to_launcher(),
    root_id="chip",
    layer_stack=get_single_die_layer_stack(),
    material_records=get_material_records(),
    coupon_padding_um=0.0,
)
plan.set_nets({"signal": ("chip/SIGNAL",), "ground": ("chip/GROUND",)})
plan.set_vacuum_region(padding=(0.0, 0.0, 1000.0))
presets = validate_interface_preset_records()
plan.set_surface_epr({
    kind: {
        "film_thickness_m": presets[f"LiteratureCentral_{kind}"]["thickness"] * 1e-6,
        "permittivity": presets[f"LiteratureCentral_{kind}"]["permittivity"],
        "loss_tangent": presets[f"LiteratureCentral_{kind}"]["loss_tangent"],
        "source": presets[f"LiteratureCentral_{kind}"]["source"],
        "preset": f"LiteratureCentral_{kind}",
    }
    for kind in ("MA", "MS", "SA")
})

# 2. The ports: each sheet is a 50 Ω port to the ground; the left one, given first, is port 1.
plan.set_lumped_elements([
    LumpedPort("chip/o_lumped_left", reference_net="ground", impedance_ohm=50.0),
    LumpedPort("chip/o_lumped_right", reference_net="ground", impedance_ohm=50.0),
])
print("\n".join(DrivenSim.simulation_drc(plan).lumped_elements))

# 3. The sweep, 81 frequencies from 2 to 10 GHz.
sim = DrivenSim()
sim.set_plan(plan.prepare())
sim.set_output_dir(Path(".artifacts/launchers") / uuid4().hex[:12])
sim.set_driven([Linear(2e9, 10e9, points=81)], adaptive_tolerance=1e-3)

# 4. Mesh, write Palace's input, run Palace with 8 MPI processes.
sim.mesh()
sim.write_config()
handoff = sim.prepare_handoff(
    profile="direct-local",
    executable=os.environ["SCGSIM_PALACE_EXECUTABLE"],
    resources={"command_style": "wrapper", "processes": 8, "threads": 1},
)
subprocess.run(["bash", "run_palace.sh"], cwd=handoff.run_dir, check=True)

# 5. Read the S-parameters back, print them every 2 GHz and write the Touchstone file.
result = resolve_palace_result(handoff.run_dir, expected_handoff_id=handoff.handoff_id)
print("Status:", result.status)
s_params = result.driven_result()
for sampling in s_params.adaptive_sampling:
    print(
        f"Port {sampling.excited_port} driven: {sampling.samples} frequencies solved, "
        f"error {sampling.error:.1e}"
    )
s11, s21 = s_params.s(1, 1), s_params.s(2, 1)
for k, frequency in enumerate(s_params.frequencies_hz):
    if k % 20 == 0:  # every 2 GHz
        print(
            f"{frequency / 1e9:4.1f} GHz  |S11| = {20 * math.log10(abs(s11[k])):6.2f} dB"
            f"  |S21| = {20 * math.log10(abs(s21[k])):7.4f} dB"
            f"  arg S21 = {math.degrees(cmath.phase(s21[k])):8.3f} deg"
        )
s_params.write_touchstone("launchers.s2p")
```

Section 1 builds the plan as [Resonant modes with Palace](modes-palace.qmd#the-script)
does, with the same vacuum and thin films, for this layout and its two Nets,
`signal` and `ground`. What is new:

- **Section 2 declares the ports on the plan.** Each `LumpedPort` names its
  sheet, the Net of its reference conductor (the other conductor the sheet
  joins is its signal) and its impedance in ohms. The order you give them is
  the port numbering: port 1 is row and column 1 of the S-matrix. Palace
  drives each port from its signal metal to its reference, so the sense in
  which a sheet is drawn does not change the result. `simulation_drc` checks,
  in seconds and before anything is meshed, that the layout can be built
  and meshed with these ports, and reports what it makes of each: the two
  `P1` and `P2` lines of the output ([Check a layout](check-a-layout.qmd)).
  A plan without a `LumpedPort` is refused here.
- **Section 3 sets the sweep, in hertz.** `Linear(2e9, 10e9, points=81)`
  gives 81 evenly spaced frequencies, both ends included; the list can hold
  more ranges ([Dense sampling where it matters](#dense-sampling)).
  `adaptive_tolerance=1e-3` turns on
  Palace's adaptive sweep: for each port it solves the field at a few
  frequencies, builds a small model from them that it evaluates at all 81,
  and adds solves until that model agrees with them to a relative error of
  10⁻³. Here it needed 4 solves per port, where solving every frequency would
  take 81. The two `Port ... driven` lines report this; `error` is the
  model's last estimate.
- **Second-order elements, without asking.** A `DrivenSim` solves with
  second-order elements unless `set_numerical(order=...)` gives another
  order. With first-order elements, on the mesh `mesh()` writes, the phase
  the line adds comes out about 7 % too large (about 1 % at second order),
  and |S11| reaches −21.2 dB at 10 GHz instead of −29.8 dB. Second order has
  five times as many unknowns, 1,433,702 here.
- **Section 4** meshes, writes Palace's input and runs Palace, as for a
  resonator.
- **Section 5 reads the run back.** `driven_result()` returns the
  S-parameters over the plan's ports, in their order, at every frequency
  of the sweep. `s(2, 1)` is S21, the wave out of port 2 with port 1 driven,
  as a complex number at each frequency, and `s(1, 1)` is S11.
  `write_touchstone` writes the record as a Touchstone 1.1 file, in GHz with
  |S| in dB and arg S in degrees, referenced to the ports' 50 Ω; its suffix
  must be `.s2p` for two ports.

Run it from the study project, in the shell where you set
`SCGSIM_PALACE_EXECUTABLE`:

```bash
uv run launcher_s_parameters.py
```

With 8 MPI processes it took about six minutes on a workstation, and Palace
used up to 14 GB of memory.

## Read the result {#read-the-result}

The numbers follow one convention:

- **At the port sheets.** The values are at the sheets behind the pads, with
  nothing removed, so they include both pads and both tapers: they describe
  the chip from one launcher's landing to the other's.
- **Against each port's own impedance.** Each port's waves are measured
  against its own impedance, 50 Ω here, with the other port terminated in
  its 50 Ω.
- **Signed by the reference Net.** Each port runs from its signal metal to
  the metal of its `reference_net`, here `ground`. Turning one port around
  would turn S21 and S12 by 180° and leave S11 and S22 as they are.
- **A delay is a falling phase.** As the frequency rises, the phase of a
  through line's S21 falls: here by about 5.56° per GHz.

**Transmission.** |S21| is −0.0004 dB at 2 GHz and −0.0058 dB at
10 GHz: nearly all the power goes through. The only lossy material is the
silicon, with a loss tangent of 2.6 × 10⁻⁷, so the power that neither comes
back nor goes through, 1 − |S11|² − |S21|², should be close to zero; it is
at most 2.9 × 10⁻⁴ over the band.

**The reflection.** The CPW's characteristic impedance, from conformal
mapping, is about 54.4 Ω, not 50 Ω, so each end reflects a little:
Γ = (54.37 − 50)/(54.37 + 50) = 0.042. The two reflections of a 900 µm line
alone would give |S11| ≈ 2Γ|sin βL|, −42.0 dB at 2 GHz and −28.3 dB at
10 GHz. Palace gives −41.1 and −29.8 dB, the same size: the launchers
reflect too, and part of their reflection cancels the line's, so the
estimate gives the size of |S11|, not its value.

**The delay.** The fall of 5.559° per GHz is a delay of 15.44 ps. The
line accounts for 7.57 ps (900 µm at an effective index of 2.5212); the two
launchers, with their pads and tapers, for the other 7.87 ps.

**Reciprocity and symmetry.** S12 equals S21 to 7.7 × 10⁻¹⁵, as it must for
a reciprocal device, and the layout is mirror-symmetric, so S11 and S22
should be equal: they differ by at most 1.6 × 10⁻⁴.

## Surface participation {#surface-participation}

A driven run also computes, at each frequency and with each port driven,
the share of the electric energy that sits in each thin film of
`set_surface_epr`: its participation p. `s_params.surface_epr` holds one
record per driven port and frequency, 162 here, in port order and then sweep
order:

```python
epr = s_params.surface_epr[0]  # port 1 driven, at 2 GHz
for row in epr.surfaces:
    print(row.name, f"p = {row.participation:.3e}")
```

This prints, for port 1 driven at 2 GHz:

```text
MA::chip/GROUND__sidewall p = 5.399e-08
MA::chip/GROUND__top p = 3.887e-07
MA::chip/SIGNAL__sidewall p = 1.280e-07
MA::chip/SIGNAL__top p = 1.085e-06
MS::chip/GROUND__bottom p = 4.615e-05
MS::chip/SIGNAL__bottom p = 1.314e-04
SA::D0_SUBSTRATE|VACUUM_REGION__interface p = 1.558e-04
```

The metal–substrate (MS) and substrate–air (SA) films hold the most, and the
metal–air (MA) films about a hundred times less. These rows are the ones a resonator study of the same plan reports
([Surface EPR](../concepts/surface-epr.qmd#rows)), but a driven
participation is the energy stored at one frequency with one port driven,
not a mode's. Only near an isolated resonance does it approach the mode's
participation, so SCGSim derives no Q or T1 from it. A film's
`inset_margins_um` adds margin rows in `epr.margins`, as for a resonator
([Surface EPR near the gaps](modes-palace.qmd#surface-epr-margin-rows)).

## Settings you may change {#settings-you-may-change}

- **A full solve at every frequency.** Leave out `adaptive_tolerance` and
  Palace solves every frequency once per port. That is 162 solves for this
  sweep, about 37 s each at second order on this chip; choose it for a few
  frequencies, or to check the adaptive sweep at some of them. On this chip
  at first order, the adaptive sweep agreed with the full solves at 2, 4, 6,
  8 and 10 GHz to 3 × 10⁻⁵° in arg S21 and 2 × 10⁻⁴ dB in |S11|.

  ::: {.callout-note title="High-Q resonances and full solves"}
  Full solves through a high-Q resonance need a tighter linear-solver
  tolerance than the default 10⁻⁶: `set_numerical(tolerance=1e-9)`. The
  adaptive sweep is accurate at the default, so the default stays 10⁻⁶.
  [Full solves at the default tolerance](frequency-sweeps-palace.qmd#full-solves-at-the-default-tolerance)
  shows what the default gave on a hanger resonator.
  :::
- **The adaptive sweep's limit.** `adaptive_max_samples` caps the solves per
  port; without it Palace's own cap of 20 applies. When a port reaches the
  cap before the model agrees to the tolerance, Palace's log says so and
  `driven_result()` refuses the run, naming the port: run again with a
  larger cap.
- **More ports, or other elements.** Give as many `LumpedPort`s as the
  layout has sheets; port i is the i-th you give, and every port is driven
  in turn. `write_touchstone` needs one impedance for all ports, as
  Touchstone 1.1 references every port to one. A `LumpedElement` on the
  plan beside the ports, a junction's inductance say, is solved as a load
  with its R, L and C and is never driven; the S-matrix has rows only for
  the ports, so one port and one element give a one-port result and an
  `.s1p` file ([Lumped elements](../reference/specs/geometry-plan.qmd#lumped-elements)).
- **Mesh refinement.** Palace runs on the mesh `mesh()` writes unless you
  enable refinement with `set_numerical(amr_max_passes=..., amr_update_fraction=...)`.
  Each pass solves the sweep again. To compare mesh passes as in HFSS, give a
  few explicit frequencies, for example `sim.set_driven([Points([2e9, 6e9, 10e9])])`.
  With `adaptive_tolerance` omitted, Palace solves every port in full at
  each of these frequencies. Run a dense frequency sweep separately.

  Import `Points` and `SMatrix` from `scgsim.palace`. Declare Maximum Delta S
  with `sim.set_convergence(SMatrix().within(delta_s=delta_s_limit))` and
  leave `amr_tolerance` unset. From pass 2, SCGSim compares complex
  S-parameters at matching frequencies on successive passes. The criterion
  holds when the largest absolute difference across all frequencies and matrix
  entries is below the `delta_s_limit` you chose.
  `ErrorIndicator().below(...)` checks Palace's own error estimate. For
  Palace's native stopping rule, set `amr_tolerance` without a convergence
  declaration. To read the verdict of a declaration, see
  [Convergence and reports](convergence-and-reports.qmd#declare-convergence).
- **The outer boundary.** The faces of the vacuum region get no boundary
  condition, which Palace treats as a perfect magnetic conductor, as for a
  resonator: the model is a closed box with almost no loss. Such a box has
  resonances of its own, and on a large chip they can fall inside the
  sweep, where they show in the S-parameters as features the device does
  not have.
- **Metal as sheets.** Call `sim.set_route("A")` before `mesh()` to use the
  [sheet approximation](capacitance-palace.qmd#select-the-geometry-approximation-and-build-inputs).
  The mesher sizes the conductor-sheet edges using the metal thickness from
  the stack. In the launcher-to-launcher example, the two routes' S21 phases
  differed by at most 0.2° at 2, 6 and 10 GHz.
  [Route comparison](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/309#issuecomment-7193230531)
- **HFSS.** [S-parameters with HFSS](s-parameters-hfss.qmd) declares two
  ports the same way for HFSS Driven Terminal, on a plan without Surface
  EPR.

### Dense sampling where it matters {#dense-sampling}

`set_driven` takes a list of ranges in hertz, and Palace solves at all of
their frequencies together, in order, each frequency once. To resolve a
narrow feature, a resonance near 7.32 GHz say, give the band coarsely and a
window around the feature densely:

```python
sim.set_driven(
    [
        Linear(4e9, 9e9, points=501),  # the band, 10 MHz apart
        Linear(7.30e9, 7.34e9, points=4001),  # the window, 10 kHz apart
    ],
    adaptive_tolerance=1e-3,
)
```

That is 4,497 frequencies: the band's five from 7.30 to 7.34 GHz are also
the window's, and each is solved once. `Log(start, stop, points=...)`
spaces its points evenly on a log scale, for a band of several decades, and
`Points([...])` lists chosen frequencies; all three come from
`scgsim.palace` and can be mixed in one list. Two frequencies must be the
same or more than 10 Hz apart, 1 Hz below 1 GHz and 100 Hz from 10 GHz up:
Palace takes frequencies less than 1 Hz apart as one and prints each with
nine significant digits, so closer ones are refused. An adaptive sweep
needs at least three frequencies. Which sweep to choose for what you want
to compute, and what a sweep costs, is in
[Choose a frequency sweep with Palace](frequency-sweeps-palace.qmd).

A range given `full_solve=True` is solved in full at each of its
frequencies, once per port, before the adaptive sweep chooses solves of its
own, and its model is built from those solves too. A resonance found with
[Resonant modes with Palace](modes-palace.qmd) is one such frequency:

```python
sim.set_driven(
    [
        Linear(4e9, 9e9, points=501),
        Linear(7.30e9, 7.34e9, points=4001),
        Points([7.3566e9], full_solve=True),  # solved in full
    ],
    adaptive_tolerance=1e-3,
)
```

`full_solve` works on `Linear`, `Log` and `Points`, and only in an adaptive
sweep: without `adaptive_tolerance` every frequency is solved in full
already, and `set_driven` refuses it. The full solves count toward
`adaptive_max_samples`, or Palace's cap of 20, together with the two at the
lowest and the highest frequency, so a cap below them is refused. A
full-solve frequency that falls on a frequency of another range is that
frequency once. Palace may then compute the other range's frequency lower
by a rounding error, keep it instead and stop as it starts, naming the
full-solve frequency: move it more than 10 Hz away then.
